newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RTRS-AMP targets NZ's rural lending market, cuts rates.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AMP targets NZ's rural lending market, cuts rates.

text.p: AMP set a new floating rate for rural loans of 9.95 percent in a move to re-establish itself as a lender to the farming sector, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Friday.
The Australasian financial services group, which has expanded into the mortgage lending market in the last year, said it was moving aggressively into the rural lending market.

The new floating rate was the lowest since February 1995, while fixed term rural loans have also dropped, to 9.5 percent for one year and 9.65 percent for both two and three year terms. "AMP is moving to re-establish itself as a leading provider of financial services to farmers," said Ross Baker, Manager of Customer Marketing for AMP New Zealand. The new rates are effective immediately for new loans and will take effect on 1 March for existing loans.
